<translate>
'''Modding''' covers everything you can add to or change in DragonMineZ without writing Java code. Races, transformations, sagas, side quests, wishes, NPC conversations, [[Special:MyLanguage/Space Pod|Space Pod]] destinations, weapon movesets, models and textures are all read from JSON files and resource packs: you edit them with a text editor, reload them and test them in game.
</translate>

<translate>
If this is your first time, start with [[Special:MyLanguage/How to JSON|How to JSON]] and [[Special:MyLanguage/Locating Specific Folders|Locating Specific Folders]]. To write your own Forge mod that hooks into DragonMineZ, see [[Special:MyLanguage/Add-on Development|Add-on Development]] instead.
</translate>

<translate>
== Data or code ==
</translate>
<translate>
There are two ways to extend DragonMineZ. Everything in this section of the wiki is a data add-on; code add-ons are covered in [[Special:MyLanguage/Add-on Development|Add-on Development]].
</translate>

{| class="wikitable"
! <translate>Approach</translate> !! <translate>What you need</translate> !! <translate>Where to start</translate>
|-
| <translate>'''Data add-ons''': configs, races, forms, quests, wishes, Dragon Ball packs and resource packs</translate> || <translate>A text editor and a DragonMineZ instance</translate> || {{L|How to JSON}}
|-
| <translate>'''Code add-ons''': your own Forge mod that hooks DragonMineZ events and APIs</translate> || <translate>A Forge 1.20.1 development environment</translate> || {{L|Add-on Getting Started}}
|}

<translate>
DragonMineZ has no Java API to register new races, forms, skills or techniques: new races and forms are always added through JSON config files.
</translate>

<translate>
== Where each kind of content lives ==
</translate>
{{Main|Locating Specific Folders}}
<translate>
* Tuning stats, damage or costs, or adding a race, form, entity or raid: <code>config/dragonminez/</code>
* Adding or editing story content, wishes, dialogue or NPC placement for one world: <code><world save>/dragonminez/</code>
* Shipping a distributable Dragon Ball pack: <code><game dir>/dragonballs/</code>
* Space Pod destinations, weapon attributes and rhythm charts: a datapack
* Adding a model, texture or animation: <code>assets/dragonminez/...</code> in a resource pack
</translate>

<translate>
== Applying your changes ==
</translate>
{{Main|Reloading and Updating Changes}}
<translate>
Each kind of file is applied in a different way. <code>/dmzreload</code> with no argument reloads everything it covers.
</translate>

{| class="wikitable"
! <translate>Content</translate> !! <translate>How to apply it</translate>
|-
| <translate>Races, forms, NPC placements and NPC alignment rules</translate> || {{Command|/dmzreload config}}
|-
| <translate>Sagas, quests, side quests and NPC dialogue</translate> || {{Command|/dmzreload story}}
|-
| <translate>Per-world wish lists</translate> || {{Command|/dmzreload wishes}}
|-
| <translate>Space Pod destinations, weapon attributes and structure NPCs</translate> || <translate>Vanilla <code>/reload</code></translate>
|-
| <translate>Wish lists inside Dragon Ball packs</translate> || <translate>Vanilla <code>/reload</code>, then <code>/dmzreload wishes</code></translate>
|-
| <translate>New dragons, ball sets and radars</translate> || <translate>Restart the game</translate>
|-
| <translate>Models, textures and animations</translate> || <translate>Resource reload ({{Key|F3}} + {{Key|T}}) or restart</translate>
|}

<translate>
== Translating your content ==
</translate>
<translate>
All in-game text uses translation keys. Races, forms, sagas, quests, wishes and dialogue lines take a translation key wherever a name or a text is shown, and each page of this section lists the key pattern it uses. Add your keys to your <code>en_us.json</code> or to your own language file in a resource pack (<code>assets/<namespace>/lang/<locale>.json</code>). You don't need to add translation keys for anything else: DragonMineZ merges the translations already made on Crowdin with your own.
</translate>
